demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Dates or anniversaries connected to the event
become overly compliant when feeling threatened
Driving or being a passenger in a vehicle

Threat.value: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger
When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief

Negative Appraisals.value: I can't rely on other people
I can no longer trust my own body
I should have protected others and I failed

issues.item: Animal Phobia: Talks or photos about snakes
issues.explanation: 'Talks or photos about snakes' is hard to reconcile with the stated trauma type of accidentally causing serious injury to another unless the accident specifically involved a snake, which is not suggested anywhere else in the profile. The other trigger items point to generic post-traumatic cueing, but this item implies a highly specific trauma cue that lacks support from the rest of the formulation.

issues.item: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: 'I was betrayed by someone I trusted' does not fit well with the trauma type of accidentally causing serious injury to another and is not supported by the other nodes. The profile otherwise centers on guilt, danger scanning, intrusive recollection, and distrust of self/body; betrayal by another person introduces a different interpersonal trauma theme without corroboration.

issues.item: Avoid Intimacy: Being emotionally close or intimate with others
issues.explanation: Avoiding emotional closeness/intimacy is weakly supported by the rest of the profile. The dominant threat and memory items concern danger, hypervigilance, intrusive imagery, numbness, and grief after an accidental injury event. Intimacy avoidance could occur, but here it appears to address an interpersonal/betrayal theme that is not otherwise coherently represented, especially given the unsupported betrayal appraisal.

issues.item: Threat: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
issues.explanation: The threat profile is dominated by generalized interpersonal/environmental danger monitoring (avoiding unfamiliar places, scanning exits in any room), which fits assault or deliberate threat contexts better than accidentally causing serious injury to another in an accident. For this trauma type, threat is more plausibly focused on accidents, loss of control, or harm recurrence rather than pervasive escape-oriented vigilance across all settings.

issues.item: Threat: Scanning Exits: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
issues.explanation: The appraisal 'I can't rely on other people' is weakly grounded in the rest of the profile. The other nodes center on accident-related triggers, guilt, bodily unreliability, and generalized hypervigilance, but there is no corresponding interpersonal betrayal, abandonment, or dependence theme to support this item. It stands out as clinically disconnected from the trauma narrative and the rest of the selected items.

vignette: Thuy was nineteen when a client’s sudden shift caused her to drop a heavy ceramic mixing bowl. The violent crack against the tile floor still jolts her chest, instantly pulling her into a vivid, inescapable crash imagery that feels indistinguishable from a highway pileup. Each time that auditory shock strikes, her body locks into a frantic physical reactivity, heart hammering and breath shortening as if the danger were actively unfolding. That relentless physiological alarm never fades, which leaves her convinced that her own body is fundamentally unreliable, betraying her at the worst possible moment. Fearing another catastrophe, she began steering clear of any vehicle and marking calendar dates connected to the event with dread, while her salon clients quickly noticed her increasingly compliant, fawning demeanor whenever tension arose. The more she retreated into avoidance and appeasement, the more her nervous system stayed permanently wired, which in turn made her more susceptible to the sudden jolts of the past. The tighter she clung to control, the less she believed she could rely on others to keep her safe, a conviction that only made her scan for exits the moment she entered any new room. That constant hypervigilance stripped her memories of emotion, leaving her feeling numb, yet when the grief finally overpowered the numbness, it reinforced her crushing belief that she had failed to protect the person she loved. Working behind the styling chair, Thuy found that the sight of a hot iron still triggered a rush of phantom brake lights, which then deepened her sense of bodily unreliability and forced her into an even more desperate fawn response to neutralize any perceived threat. Her attempts to suppress the past by avoiding driving only left the visual memories more vivid, while her relentless scanning for escape routes kept her physically reactive and unable to relax, which made her memories surface as overwhelming grief rather than detached fragments. The more she numbed herself to the pain, the more those frozen images returned, which cemented her conviction that she was fundamentally broken and entirely alone in her recovery. This isolation made her flinch harder at every loud noise, as the sensory flashes bypassed her defenses and directly triggered her physical alarm. Her fawning compliance drained her energy, which only amplified her negative appraisals about her own incompetence, ensuring that every new trigger felt like proof of her failure. Even her avoidance of anniversaries left her hyperalert to calendar shifts, which fed back into her negative appraisals and kept her scanning for threats in a loop she could no longer step out of. The constant physiological arousal left her unable to wind down, which pushed her further into avoidance and appeasement as the only viable coping mechanism. Her belief that she was fundamentally broken made her recall the event in detached, emotionless fragments, as if the pain belonged to someone else. Over the following months, the salon floor became a minefield of sensory reminders. Every clatter of ceramic bowls or sharp snap of sectioning clips sent her into a state of paralysis, where the sudden auditory shock would instantly pull her back into the crash imagery of that afternoon. Because she could not relax even in her own home, her physical reactivity remained permanently elevated, which guaranteed that any new trigger would hijack her nervous system before she could process it. The more she retreated into avoidance and appeasement, the more her nervous system stayed permanently wired, which in turn made her more susceptible to the sudden jolts of the past. Her attempts to control the environment by appeasing others only exhausted her nervous system, leaving her perpetually wired and more likely to misread a dropped phone ring as a siren. The tighter she clung to control, the less she believed she could rely on others, a conviction that only made her scan for exits the moment she entered any new room. Her relentless scanning for escape routes kept her physically reactive and unable to relax, which made her memories surface as overwhelming grief rather than detached fragments. The constant physiological arousal left her unable to wind down, which pushed her further into avoidance and appeasement as the only viable coping mechanism. Her belief that she was fundamentally broken made her recall the event in detached, emotionless fragments, as if the pain belonged to someone else. This isolation made her flinch harder at every loud noise, as the sensory flashes bypassed her defenses and directly triggered her physical alarm. Her fawning compliance drained her energy, which only amplified her negative appraisals about her own incompetence, ensuring that every new trigger felt like proof of her failure. Even her avoidance of anniversaries left her hyperalert to calendar shifts, which fed back into her negative appraisals and kept her scanning for threats. The constant physiological arousal left her unable to wind down, which pushed her further into avoidance and appeasement as the only viable coping mechanism. It took six months of sleepless nights and a fractured relationship with her boyfriend before Thuy finally sat in the intake room at the community clinic. She no longer trusts the quiet of her own apartment, and she has come to the therapist hoping to understand why her body continues to scream danger when nothing is actually wrong. She fears that if she stops monitoring for threats, she will inevitably cause another tragedy, and she desperately wants to reclaim the steady, grounded presence she had before the bowl fell.
